note.p: Mrs. Wood was the daughter of Cossley Hall of Hyde Hall in Jamaica. Her sister was Miss Mary Cossley Hall who died in 1844. Mrs. Woods originally married a Mr. Green (also from Jamaica) by whom she had a daughter who became Mrs. Leicester Stanhope. After her marriage to Mr. Wood she became as society hostess, whom Godwin and Mary Shelley saw a good deal between 1831 and 1835. She was famous for large parties with unusual people, and a large measure of foreigners!
The entries for 1796 and 1804 have not been coded as Mrs. Wood. 'Wood' appearing with Gaskell and Stanhope has been taken to be a shorthand reference to Mrs. Wood and coded accordingly.
